Photograph: James Veysey/Shutterstock Weather tracker Environment Analysis Temperatures to fall across Europe as substantial rain heading for parts of UK Jodie Woodcock for MetDesk Temperatures could drop by more than 15C compared with last Thursday as cold front moves arrives from Monday Mon 17 Aug 2026 05.37 EDT Last modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 05.52 EDT Share Relief from the unrelenting heat is finally arriving this week across western Europe , with more unsettled conditions bringing the chance of rain. Temperatures are expected to fall back towards the seasonal norm, with some parts of the UK even falling about 3C below normal by Thursday. After such a scorching summer, and with a temperature drop of more than 15C compared with last Thursday’s heat, it may feel surprisingly chilly. There are signs that some substantial rain could be on the cards for the south of the UK this week as a cold front moves in from the Atlantic on Monday night into Tuesday. As of Monday, parts of southern England had endured 62 consecutive days of no rainfall – this is observed at a Met Office weather station in Wisley, Surrey. Even the last recorded rainfall here on 16 June amounted to just 0.4mm. The more interesting weather arrives from Wednesday into the weekend, as low pressure moves across the UK, bringing frequent sharp showers and potentially thundery downpours. After such a prolonged dry spell, even a few substantial bursts of rain will make a noticeable difference to the environment. Continental Europe is also likely to turn wetter as the main cold front sinks southwards into France and Germany on Wednesday. Farther south, however, rainfall is likely to be more hit and miss, relying heavily on showers and thunderstorms, with this risk really rising from Thursday. While the heat is subsiding on this side of the Atlantic, the southern US states have extended extreme heat warnings this week. There is a significant lack of overnight cooling and relief from the heat, with overnight lows not falling much below 27-28C (low 80sF). For perspective, the UK’s highest overnight minimum during the late June heatwave reached about 22-23C. High humidity is also contributing to the uncomfortable conditions and is helping push the heat index to such high levels to warrant the extreme heat warnings. The combination of air temperature and humidity produces the heat index, or apparent temperature, which better reflects how hot conditions feel. Apparent temperatures of 31-33C are being modelled as the overnight lows, with the National Weather Service warning of “dangerously hot conditions” as the forecasted daytime heat index values could exceed 46C, especially across Louisiana and Mississippi. Photograph: World Discovery/Alamy View image in fullscreen Tokyo’s popular Shinjuku ward is introducing bans on short-term visitor accommodation such as Airbnb after complaints about tourists’ behaviour. Photograph: World Discovery/Alamy Japan Tokyo tourist hotspot bans short-term rentals amid surge in complaints Shinjuku ward targets accommodation in residential areas and near cultural sites as locals complain visitors disposing of rubbish improperly and being too noisy Justin McCurry in Tokyo Tue 8 Sep 2026 03.43 EDT First published on Tue 8 Sep 2026 01.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A neighbourhood in Tokyo popular with foreign tourists will ban visitors from using thousands of short-term rental accommodations after a slew of complaints about behaviour. In the latest sign that Japan’s patience with mass tourism is wearing thin, Shinjuku ward – home to the notorious Kabukicho nightlife district and the world’s busiest railway station – will prevent visitors from using private lodgings in residential areas and near schools and important cultural sites, Japanese media reported this week. The measure, to be introduced through a local ordinance, could encourage other local authorities to follow suit. Shinjuku, with a regular population of more than 350,000, is home to 3,775 private lodgings – or minpaku – the largest number anywhere in Japan . ‘Fine for others to pay more’: can Japan attract more overseas tourists while charging them extra? Read more While tourism has boosted sectors of Japan’s economy and raised the country’s profile overseas, the surge in visitor numbers has created tensions with residents in popular destinations such as Tokyo , Kyoto and Osaka. Shinjuku ward believes the measure will affect as many as 2,000 lodgings in residential areas – almost half the total, according to the Mainichi Shimbun. The number of minpaku residences in Shinjuku has almost tripled since 2022. Reports said officials had been forced to act after receiving more than 1,300 complaints from residents in the 12 months to March. Many cited disruption caused by visitors who did not dispose of their rubbish properly, made too much noise and smoked in areas where it is banned. There have also been reports of trespassing. Officials said temporarily revoking the licenses of renters whose tenants misbehaved would not address residents’ concerns. “Even if we crack down on badly behaved operators, the number of complaints remains the same,” a ward official told the Japan Times. “So we decided it’s better to change the ordinance.” Authorities did not single out particular operators for the ban. But it is likely to affect those using popular companies such as Airbnb. An Airbnb spokesperson told the Guardian: “Shinjuku has been an important partner to us, and we take residents’ concerns seriously. Home sharing works best when residents, hosts and guests can all live well alongside each other, and that is what we want to help the ward protect. “We would welcome the chance to work with the ward on measures that target the problem more precisely - a prohibition across residential zones would close thousands of registered homes affecting compliant and responsible hosts, while leaving untouched the unregistered operators behind much of the disruption residents describe. “We believe there is a version of this ordinance that protects residents’ quality of life without closing responsible, licensed hosts, and we want to help find it.” The ward will ask for members of the public to give their feedback on the proposal next month, with a view to submitting revisions to the ordinance in February. It also plans to reduce the number of days per year that minpaku in residential areas can be rented out from 180 to 120. Authorities in Kyoto – where tourists flock to view temples and shrines, rent kimono and photograph traditional geisha entertainers – limit minpaku operations in residential areas to just 60 days a year, during the off-peak season between January and March. “Residents are concerned that their communities could be falling apart,” Kyoto’s mayor, Koji Matsui, said earlier this year. “We have strengthened the oversight of operators, but that is not enough. We need to go further,” the Asahi Shimbun quoted him as saying. A record 42 million people visited Japan last year, spending a combined ¥9.5tn ($62bn) – also an all-time high. The government has set a target of 60 million visitors by 2030 – a goal critics say will exacerbate “ tourism pollution ”. Authorities near Mount Fuji have introduced climbing fees and imposed a daily visitor cap in an attempt to reduce overcrowding on Japan’s highest mountain. In February, the town of Fujiyoshida, a popular Fuji viewing spot, decided to cancel this spring’s cherry blossom festival , citing a rise in disruptive behaviour by tourists. The mayor, Shigeru Horiuchi, said the decision had been taken to “protect the dignity and living environment of our citizens”. https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/.text: Former Sephardi Chief Rabbi Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef launched a scathing attack on Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara on Saturday night following her request to cancel or postpone a memorial rally for Rabbi Ovadia Yosef, arguing that holding the event during the election period could be considered election propaganda. “At Maran’s seven-day mourning period, nearly one million people came - secular, religious, National Religious, Hasidic and Lithuanian Jews. The entire nation of Israel was there," Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef said. “When the anniversary comes, it is only right to hold a memorial gathering in his honor, and suddenly a legal opinion is issued. That crazy woman, Miara, issues a legal opinion saying that a memorial gathering in his honor cannot be held." He concluded with a sharply personal attack: “May the Almighty destroy her and strike her with His punishment. She is going after Maran, the greatest of the generations. This will not go unanswered." Beállítom A francia zavargásokat értelmetlen rombolásnak és igazolhatatlan erőszaknak nevezve állt ki Magyar Péter a hazai szigorú migrációs fellépés, a bevándorlási politika és a határvédelem mellett. A miniszterelnök Facebookon írta azt , hogy a Franciaországban történtek miatt „talán már mindenki számára érthető, hogy Magyarország miért képviseli a lehető legszigorúbb fellépést a migráció kapcsán, és miért nem fogunk semmilyen nyomásra lazítani a külső határaink védelmén és a bevándorlási politikánkon”. Magyar azt is írta, hogy a zavargások miatt történelmi épületek semmisültek meg, több száz rendőr megsérült és óriási anyagi kár keletkezett, a történteket pedig egyre fokozódó vandalizmusnak és erőszaknak nevezte. „Legyen mindenki számára világos: a békés és jogszerű tüntetés valamint a vandalizmus és erőszak teljesen más dolog. Az első alapjog, a második pedig súlyos bűncselekmény” – írta. Azt is megjegyezte, hogy örül: a mostani uniós csúcson egyértelművé vált, hogy Európa döntő többsége felébredt, és szakítani akar a korábbi megengedő politikával. „Az az Európa, amelyet mindannyian szeretünk, ma óriási bajban van. A mi feladatunk is, hogy segítsük megőrizni a gyerekeinknek és az unokáinknak az öreg kontinenst a világ legszerethetőbb helyének. Európa számíthat Magyarországra” – tette hozzá, majd megjegyezte, hogy teljes szolidaritását fejezi ki a francia nemzettel. Szombaton erőszakos cselekményekre került sor Franciaország több városában is a békésnek induló tüntetéseken. A rendőrség mintegy 1200 embert vett őrizetbe, a becslések szerint 550 ezren vonultak az utcákra. Sébastien Lecornu miniszterelnök szerint 150 rendőr megsérült a zavargások során. Magyar arról nem írt, hogy a francia tüntetések elsősorban a megélhetési gondok és az oktatásügy problémái miatt indultak. A több mint félmillió ember részvételével zajlott demonstrációk nagyrészt békésen zajlottak, de a rendőrök több városban is összecsaptak a tüntetőkkel, akik autókat és épületeket gyújtottak fel.
